newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy needs rate fall to meet deficit goal - Ispe.
newsitem.headline: Italy needs rate fall to meet deficit goal - Ispe.

text.p: Italy's deficit is set to be slightly bigger than three percent of gross domestic product (GDP) in 1997, but could still hit that target if interest rates fall, state-funded economic research institute Ispe said.
Ispe, which is tied to the budget ministry, forecast a deficit/GDP ratio of 3.2 percent for 1997, the institute's president Fiorella Padoa-Schioppa told a parliamentary committee on Tuesday.

But she said the shortfall could be covered if the government negotiated a swift, convincing reform of the welfare state. This would boost market confidence in Italy and push down interest rates, she explained.
Prime Minister Romano Prodi's centre-left government is due to start talks with union leaders later this month on a planned overhaul of the welfare state.
"A deal with the unions would have a positive impact on the market, allowing a reduction in the spread between Italian and German rates," Padoa-Schioppa said.

"A 0.4 percentage point fall in the average rate of short term bills would lower average debt servicing costs by 0.2 percentage points and as a result...reduce the deficit to three percent of GDP in 1997," she added.

However to achieve this, a welfare accord would have to be signed before the summer holidays, she stressed. Many political observers believe the complex welfare negotiations might not reach a conclusion until the autumn.

Padoa-Schioppa told the Senate budget commission that Ispe only expected GDP growth of one percent this year against the official 1.2 percent target and 1.8 percent in 1998 compared with the 2.0 percent target. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
